subject: social_science
chapter_title: Building Blocks in Economics: The Problem of Choice

concepts.title: What Economics Deals With
concepts.definition: Economics deals with the everyday problem of making a living: how people, firms and governments use scarce resources to satisfy unlimited wants, and how choices about production, exchange and consumption shape wellbeing.
concepts.key_idea: Limited means, unlimited wants: managing this gap is what economics studies.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest108.txt opening sections (what does economics deal with)
question_patterns: what does economics deal with - explain
define scarcity with an everyday example
why can wants never be fully satisfied - discuss
what are resources in economics - give examples
how do individuals and governments make economic choices
connect the problem of choice to your own daily life

solution_steps.explain: Wants outrun resources; scarcity is the starting point.
Households, firms and governments all allocate scarce means.
Choices decide what is produced, how and for whom.

concepts.title: Scarcity, Choice and Opportunity Cost
concepts.definition: Scarcity forces choice, and every choice carries an opportunity cost - the value of the next best alternative given up; choosing one use of money, time or land always means losing the chance to use it elsewhere.
concepts.key_idea: Every yes is a no: the next best thing sacrificed is the true price of a choice.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest108.txt sections on scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
question_patterns: define opportunity cost with an example
a farmer chooses wheat over cotton - what is the opportunity cost
explain the problem of choice with the given situation
why is there no free lunch in economics - justify
identify the opportunity cost in the given decisions
how does scarcity create the need for choice - explain the chain

solution_steps.explain: Money, time or land cannot serve all uses at once.
Rank the possible uses of the resource.
The highest-ranked forgone use is the opportunity cost.

concepts.title: Production, Exchange and Distribution
concepts.definition: Economic activity runs in three linked stages: production combines resources to create goods and services, exchange moves them through markets to those who need them, and distribution shares the income earned among land, labour, capital and enterprise.
concepts.key_idea: Make, trade, share: the three questions of every economy.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest108.txt sections on production, exchange and distribution
question_patterns: explain the three stages of economic activity with examples
what decides how income is distributed among factors of production
how do markets exchange goods between producers and consumers
what are goods and services - differentiate with examples
describe the production process of the given good
how does the government participate in production and distribution

solution_steps.explain: Inputs combine to create goods and services.
Markets move products to consumers through trade.
Rent, wages, interest and profit share out the earnings.
